This metric represents the monetary impact that changes in the total number of retailer customers have had on the overall sales of a product or product group between two periods. It quantifies how much of the sales growth or decline can be attributed specifically to gaining or losing customers, helping suppliers understand the role of customer base changes in overall sales performance.

This metric represents the monetary impact that changes in the total number of retailer transactions have had on the overall sales of a product or product group between two periods. It quantifies how much of the sales growth or decline can be attributed specifically to an increase or decrease in the number of transactions, helping suppliers understand the influence of transaction volume on overall sales performance.

business_name: contribution of total transactions per customer
definition: This metric represents the monetary impact that changes in the average number of transactions per customer have had on the overall sales of a product or product group between two periods. It quantifies how much of the sales growth or decline can be attributed specifically to customers purchasing more or fewer times, helping suppliers understand the effect of changes in shopping frequency on total sales performance.

This metric represents the monetary impact that changes in transaction penetration have had on the overall sales of a product or product group between two periods. Transaction penetration refers to the proportion of total retailer transactions that include the product. This metric quantifies how much of the sales growth or decline can be attributed specifically to more (or fewer) transactions including the product, helping suppliers understand the effect of product reach within the total transaction base on overall sales performance.

This metric represents the monetary impact that changes in the number of transactions have had on the overall sales of a product or product group between two periods. It quantifies how much of the sales growth or decline can be attributed specifically to an increase or decrease in transaction count, helping suppliers understand the role of transaction volume in overall sales performance.

This metric represents the monetary impact that changes in the average number of units purchased per transaction have had on the overall sales of a product or product group between two periods. It quantifies how much of the sales growth or decline can be attributed specifically to customers buying more or fewer units per transaction, helping suppliers understand the influence of basket size on total sales performance.

Formula: Gross Initial Margin = (Total Gross Receipt Retail Amount - Total Gross Receipt Cost) / Total Gross Receipt Retail Amount.

This metric provides a true measure of profitability by reflecting the impact of pricing changes and product returns on sales.Calculation:The Net Maintain Margin $ is calculated using the following formula:Net Maintain Margin $ = ((((((SUM(D) × SUM(C)) / SUM(ty_sales_amt)) / (SUM(B) - SUM(C))) × (-1)) + 1) × (SUM(B) - SUM(C))) / SUM(B)) × SUM(ty_sales_amt)Where:B = Net Sales Amount = SUM(ty_gross_rcpt_rtl_amt) - SUM(CASE WHEN RTN_SALES_AMT is NULL THEN 0 ELSE RTN_SALES_AMT END)C = Net Cost Amount = SUM(ty_gross_rcpt_cost_amt) - SUM(CASE WHEN RTN_COST_AMT is NULL THEN 0 ELSE RTN_COST_AMT END)D = Retail Adjustment = SUM(PREV_RTL_AMT - CURR_RTL_AMT)ty_sales_amt = Total Year Sales AmountDescription:Net Sales (B): Total gross receipts at retail, minus sales returns.Net Cost (C): Total gross receipts at cost, minus cost returns.Retail Adjustment (D): The sum of changes between previous and current retail amounts.

High-, Mid-, and Low-level reasons can be used to drill-down into out of stock root causes.Low-level Examples:Allocation: The item has been placed on allocation, meaning a specific volume is ordered and distributed to stores, rather than volume needed to fulfill all store demand; typically done when a supplier indicates that they cannot produce enough to fulfill all demandCID Instock: The item is out of stock, but shares a Consumer ID (CID) with another item that is instockCollect On Time Extended: The MABD for a collect order has been extended beyond the store's ability to meet customer demand with existing on handCollect On-Time: A Collect order was delivered by Walmart's supply chain to the DC after the MABDDC Capping: DC has reached its capacity and cannot receive/process/ship additional product, leading to delaysDC CWO Flag: The "Cancel When Out" Flag has been turned on at a store, which will cause the item to be move to inactive status at that store as soon as it sells through its on hand inventoryDC DeletesDC DRP: The "Do Not Replenish" flag for the item has been turned on at one or more DCsDC Dwell: Inventory sat at the DC for longer than plannedDC Markdowns: Inventory was marked down (damage, throwaway, charitable giving, etc) at the DC levelDC Manual Expire: Replenishment of item was manually expired at the DCDC Shave: DC spread orders to different days in order to manage inbound volumeDC Voids: DC made an adjustment to inventory onhand quantity (return to vendor, corrections to incorrect counts, etc)DSD In Full: The supplier did not deliver 100% of the needed volumeDynamic Distribution: A store was originally on a PO line distribution, but removed after dynamic distribution ran (i.e. something happened to cause another store to need the product more)End of Life: The item is being removed from the modular. As items draw closer to their removal date, replenishment of the item will be shut off and stores will sell through their remaining inventory. Some stores may sell out before the target removal date.EOQ: The item's Economic Order Quantity (EOQ) settings may be causing the item to under-orderEOQ-Breakpack: If the item is setup as breakpack, the vendor pack to warehouse pack ratio may be too high for too low of a rate of saleForecast: Item forecast is not keeping up with customer demandFrozen SlotsFuture DRPImport Collect On Time Ex: An Import Collect order was delivered by Walmart's supply chain to the DC after the MABDImport Collect On-Time: An Import Collect order was delivered by Walmart's supply chain to the DC after the MABDInbound Priority: Inbound priority has recently changedIn-Full Assembly: The supplier did not fulfill 100% of the ordered quantityIn-Full Staple: The supplier did not fulfill 100% of the ordered quantityLow SS with Fract Forecast: Replenishment for items with low forecasts (e.g. 0.25 units/store/week) is typically driven by safety stock. When an item like this unexpectedly sells an extra unit or two, it can cause the store to run out well ahead of the system's expectationLow Store Count: A DC is servicing less than 15 stores for the itemManual Orders: Stores created manual orders that exceeded the DC's ability to fulfill on timeMultiple Prime: An item has multiple prime item numbers at the same storeNegPI: Store made a manual adjustment downward to the onhand quantityNew DFU: A new item-store combination for this item has been created but not enough time was allotted for the flow of inventory to the storeNo Orders- Assembly: Item is setup as assembly but has not received any ordersOn-Time Prepaid: The supplier did not fulfill an order within the order delivery window (too early or too late)Other: Other out of stocks for which no apparent root cause can be identifiedPrepaid On Time Extended: The MABD for a prepaid order has been extended beyond the store's ability to meet customer demand with existing on handPrime Change: The prime item in the cross-reference chain has changed from one item to another, but not enough time was allotted for the flow of inventory to the store to reflect this changePriority Flag: Priority item (typically the prime item in the cross-reference chain) is out of stock but non-priority item in chain has inventory availablePromo Reserved: Item has inventory at a DC in Reserved Quantity despite being out of stock at storesRecall: The item has been recalledRecent Mod: The item has recently been added to the modularReturn to DC: A delivery was returned from the store to the DC (due to quality, damage, etc)Sales Outlier: Unexpected spike in salesStaple DC OutSRO: The "Stop Replenishment Only" flag has been applied to an item at a storeStore DRP: The "Do Not Replenish" flag for the item has been turned on at one or more storesStore Markdowns: Store-level markdowns generated unexpected demandStore OH Adj: Store manual adjustments reduced onhand quantity to zeroSupplier: A delivery was returned from the store to the DC (due to quality, damage, etc)Trailers On Yard: Inventory delivered to a DC stayed on the DC yard longer than plannedTrapped Inventory: Item has inventory at a DC despite being out of stock at the store; DC inventory has not moved recently - appears to be "trapped" at the DC

business_name: AUTH Based GMV Amount - Last Year
definition: GMV (Gross Merchandise Value) is the actual amount collected from the customers. The revenue collected from the customer for transactions. It's the price of items after deducting savings/discounts, and adding shipping revenue.AUTH GMV is Placed GMV excluding GMV for items cancelled because they didn't pass fraud check. This is the GMV amount based on auth based date.Note: For store channels, AUTH Based GMV, AUTH Based Net Sales, Shipped Based GMV, and Shipped Based Net Sales will all have the same value (i.e., the Net Sales amount). This amount is shown in dollars.

business_name: AUTH Based Net Sales Amount - Last Year
definition: This is the revenue recorded financially (sometimes AUTH Based Net Sales is labeled as revenue in reporting). AUTH Based Net Sales is Auth GMV except for MP (Marketplace) and services sales (In Home Services, Warranties etc.) where AUTH Based Net Sales is the commission received by Walmart. AUTH Based Net Sales is what goes on the books as actual revenue. This amount is shown in dollars.If Walmart "subsidizes" Walmart's MP prices to match the Competitor, the subsidy is also deducted from the AUTH Based Net Sales. For example, if the MP item price is $100, Walmart matches the Competitor at $90 and collects a $15 commission. Then, AUTH Based Net Sales would equal $15 (commission) - $10 (subsidy) = or in this case, $5.Note: For store channels, AUTH Based GMV, AUTH Based Net Sales, Shipped Based GMV, and Shipped Based Net Sales will all have the same value (i.e., the Net Sales amount).

The number of tab item eaches that has been received at the store on a tab invoice since the last tab date. It is also called the Tab.Additional information: Tab is a type of promotion where Walmart puts a multi-page flyer in the newspaper/digital version (top of specific store’s page in [walmart.com/app](http://walmart.com/app)) that features products to customers. It runs for certain duration. When an item is “put on Tab” there is an increase in demand at the store for that item. To accommodate for that temporary increase in demand, suppliers are often asked to ship in a special shipment of merchandise into the stores (via the distribution centers (DC)) that the store holds in the backroom and can replenish the shelves with as the item sells more quickly. To separate the normal flow of inventory into the store from the inventory marked for the Tab promotion, this field is used.

Must Arrive by Date (MABD) is a date included on every purchase order (PO). It is the date on which the order is expected to arrive at the Walmart Distribution Center (DC) or Fulfillment Center (FC). For (Direct Store Delivery) DSD suppliers, this is the date on which the order is expected to arrive at the Walmart store.Must Arrive by Date (MABD) is determined by the Walmart system and is driven by when the product is needed in the store. Based on when the product is needed in the store, the system calculates when the product needs to ship from the DC and therefore the date it must be received at the DC. Using this Must Arrive by Date (MABD), the system determines when the order needs to be placed at the supplier based on the lead time setting that is in the system to ship from the supplier’s ship point to the Walmart DC placing the order.Note:The header MABD Date will usually match the line MABD. However, in very small occurrences, the two can be different. This can occur when a PO (Purchase Order) has a large number of items spread across multiple truck loads. In these instances, the header MABD Date will always display the last chronological (or max) value.For example, if a PO has 2 lines one with 7/1/2022 as an MABD and 8/6/2022 as the other MABD, the header will list 8/6/2022 as the MABD.

business_name: GMROII (Gross Margin Return On Inventory Investment)
definition: GMROII measures the amount of gross profit dollars annually generated for each dollar on inventory purchased. In other words, it is a measure of how efficiently the inventory is deployed to produce gross profit. It is optimized by either increasing initial margin or minimizing inventory and investment in inventory which increases turns.

It is the gross profit percentage after markup/markdown is applied.Gross Maintained Margin is calculated using the gross initial margin % and the markdown %, instead of dollars. It does not account for changes in inventory levels, but only for the interaction of the gross initial margin % and markdowns. It's one of the most commonly used store profitability metrics.
It is the mark up and markdown dollars expressed as percentage of sale.

Net Maintain Margin % measures the profit percentage after accounting for all markups, markdowns, and returns. This metric reflects the true profitability as a percentage of sales, incorporating the effects of price changes and product returns. Calculation:The Net Maintain Margin % is calculated using the following formula:Net Maintain Margin % = ((((((SUM(PREV_RTL_AMT - CURR_RTL_AMT) × SUM(C)) / SUM(ty_sales_amt)) / (SUM(B) - SUM(C))) × (-1)) + 1) × (SUM(B) - SUM(C)) ) / SUM(B)) × 100Where:B = Net Sales AmountSUM(ty_gross_rcpt_rtl_amt) - SUM(CASE WHEN RTN_SALES_AMT is NULL THEN 0 ELSE RTN_SALES_AMT END)C = Net Cost AmountSUM(ty_gross_rcpt_cost_amt) - SUM(CASE WHEN RTN_COST_AMT is NULL THEN 0 ELSE RTN_COST_AMT END)ty_sales_amt = Total Year Sales AmountPREV_RTL_AMT and CURR_RTL_AMT = Previous and Current Retail AmountsDescription:Net Sales (B): Total gross receipts at retail, minus sales returns.Net Cost (C): Total gross receipts at cost, minus cost returns.Retail Adjustment (D): The sum of changes between previous and current retail amounts.

Values of Rule\_ID are listed below: \- RFIDADJ: The RFIDadj values are inventory adjustments that are due to the RFID program.\- Set To Zero (STZ): If the item has an on-hand of less than two case packs and has no activity (sales, receiving, etc) in the last 3 days and has at least 2 out events then set the on-hand to 0. \- OSO (also known as XSX): If the item had an out scan in the last 90 days followed by a receiving and sell through of the entire receiving quantity (+/- 2) AND the on-hand from the prior out scan is within 2 of the current on-hand then set the on-hand to 0. \- LTO (SOAR-like logic, short-term out - NEW): If the item has at least 3 out scans, has been on our list daily for 7 days and is not on order then set the on-hand to 0. \- LTO (SOAR-like logic, long-term out - NEW): If the item has at least 3 out scans and has been on our list daily for 14 days then set the on-hand to 0.

Average Unit Retail (AUR) is the average selling price per unit of items sold before any savings, discounts, or shipping revenues are applied. It is calculated by dividing the total gross merchandise value (GMV, excluding discounts and shipping) by the total number of units sold. An increase in AUR may indicate higher sales of premium-priced items, while a decrease could signal more sales of lower-priced items or pricing adjustments in the market.This data is specific to Delivery channel.

business_name: AUTH Based Net Sales Amount - This Year
definition: This is the revenue recorded financially (sometimes AUTH Based Net Sales is labeled as revenue in reporting). AUTH Based Net Sales is Auth GMV except for MP (Marketplace) and services sales (In Home Services, Warranties etc.) where AUTH Based Net Sales is the commission received by Walmart. AUTH Based Net Sales is what goes on the books as actual revenue. This amount is shown in dollars.If Walmart "subsidizes" Walmart's MP prices to match the Competitor, the subsidy is also deducted from the AUTH Based Net Sales. For example, if the MP item price is $100, Walmart matches the Competitor at $90 and collects a $15 commission. Then, AUTH Based Net Sales would equal $15 (commission) - $10 (subsidy) = or in this case, $5.Note: For store channels, AUTH Based GMV, AUTH Based Net Sales, Shipped Based GMV, and Shipped Based Net Sales will all have the same value (i.e., the Net Sales amount).
